From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Discovery Recap: Data privacy & logging constraints

Hi Aisha / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the outcomes and next steps so we’re aligned. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, and immediate asks from your security/compliance perspective.

Pain points & constraints we heard
- Customer prompts and some enrichment data contain PII (names, emails, SSNs in rare cases).
- Regulatory retention window: Acme needs audit logs and data retention capability for up to 13 months (VA request: 13 months) and ability to shorten retention for certain datasets.
- Auditability: you require immutable audit logs with user/action/timestamp and ability to export for audits.
- Redaction: automated redaction or tokenization for known sensitive fields before they hit model logs. Manual redaction workflows for flagged records.
- Data residency: primary US-only residency for production data; staging in US as well.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest/in-transit, KMS integration, and a DPA.

Success criteria (what will make a POC successful)
1) PII redaction/tokenization in ingest pipeline demonstrable in 2-week POC
2) Audit log export with required fields and 30/90/365 retention controls (configurable per route)
3) Policy to disable model logging or enable strict sampling for sensitive routes
4) Evidence of SOC2 and a signed DPA/contract terms

Immediate next steps
- I’ll share our filled security questionnaire and a sample audit log schema (attached).
- Schedule a follow-up deep-dive with your security team next week (please confirm availability Wed/Thu).
- Laura will share SOC2 evidence and DPA language.
- Rishi and I will draft a proposed 2-week POC plan and mutual action plan (MAP) and send a draft MSA for redlines.

Attachments: redwood_security_questionnaire_responses.pdf (answers), audit_log_schema_example.csv (example schema), soc2-report-link.txt (link to SOC2 evidence).

If any of the above is inaccurate or missing, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll book the security call once you confirm availability.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@acmeanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Data privacy & logging constraints

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention: we need the ability to retain logs for up to 13 months for regulated product lines. For non-regulated product lines we want a shorter default (30 days) and the ability to configure per-route.
- Redaction: automated field-level redaction for PCI/SSN/email and an API to apply custom redaction rules would be ideal.
- Audit logs: schema looks good from the example; can you confirm whether logs are immutable and if exports are available via S3? We also need a retention toggle in the Console (not just via support ticket).
- Evidence: please share SOC2 Type II report and a copy of the DPA. Our legal team will also want MSA redlines. I’ve attached our standard security questionnaire for you to review.

Availability: Wed 2026-09-02 10:00–12:00 PDT works for our security lead (I can block 10:30).

Next steps for you: send the security artifacts and draft MAP/POC timeline. We’ll review DPA/MSA and provide redlines.

Regards,
Aisha Khan
Director of Product Security
Acme Analytics
aisha.k@acmeanalytics.com
